title: Manchester City want €80 million to sell Rodri to Real Madrid -report
summary: Real Madrid have reportedly targeted Rodri, but Manchester City demand €80 million while Real's bid is capped at €60 million. Rodri, whose contract expires in 2027, is keen to leave and negotiations between the clubs must conclude in the coming weeks if a move is to happen before next season.
content:
Real Madrid have decided to go after Rodri Hernández, but Manchester City want at least €80 million to let the Spanish midfielder go, according to a report from Es Radio’s Sergio Valentin. On the other hand, Real Madrid has capped its offer for the 2026 World Cup Golden Ball winner at €60 million, so the two clubs will have to negotiate.

Rodri is determined to leave Manchester City for both personal and football reasons. Real Madrid have leverage considering that Rodri’s contract is set to expire in the summer of 2027, but the clubs will have to reach some sort of agreement during the next few weeks if Rodri wants to be a Madrid player next season.

## Transfer battle for Rodri

Real Madrid have decided to go after Rodri Hernández, but Manchester City want at least €80 million to let the Spanish midfielder go, according to a report from Es Radio’s Sergio Valentin. On the other hand, Real Madrid has capped its offer for the 2026 World Cup Golden Ball winner at €60 million, so the two clubs will have to negotiate.

Rodri is determined to leave Manchester City for both personal and football reasons. Real Madrid have leverage considering that Rodri’s contract is set to expire in the summer of 2027, but the clubs will have to reach some sort of agreement during the next few weeks if Rodri wants to be a Madrid player next season.

## Negotiation details

- Manchester City valuation: at least €80 million  
- Real Madrid’s capped offer: €60 million  
- Rodri’s contract expires: summer 2027  
- Timeline: clubs need to negotiate in the next few weeks  
- Motivation: Rodri is determined to leave for personal and football reasons  
- Source: Es Radio’s Sergio Valentin
